questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

He flatters the boss to his face but criticises him __in his absence__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. 'behind his back'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"behind his back"** means to do something without someone's knowledge, typically in a deceitful or sneaky manner. (पीठ पीछे)

 
 
• **Example:** She found out that they had been talking about her behind her back.
 
 
 
• **"behind his back"** is an idiom that implies actions or words that are kept secret from the person concerned and are usually negative or critical. (पीठ पीछे)
 
 
• **Example:** He was upset when he learned that his friends were making fun of him behind his back.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. 'behind his back'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **At random** (बिना किसी क्रम के): Without a specific pattern, order, or objective.

 
 
• **Example:** The winner was chosen at random from a list of participants.
 
 
 
• **Behind the scenes** (पर्दे के पीछे): In secret, especially in a way that is not public knowledge.
 
 
• **Example:** Many negotiations took place behind the scenes before the deal was finalized.
 
 
 
• **At home** (घर पर): In one's own residence.
 
 
• **Example:** She prefers to work at home rather than in an office.

questions.question:
Directions: Given below are some idioms/phrases followed by four alternative meanings to each. Select the response (a), (b), (c) or (d), which is the most appropriate meaning and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly. 

Have the last laugh

options.text: to be the worst example of something
to succeed when others thought that you would not
to solve all the problems of life

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"have the last laugh"** means:

 
 
• To succeed when others thought that you would not. (अंत में सफल होना जब दूसरे सोचते थे कि आप सफल नहीं होंगे)
 
 
 
• **Example:** Despite all the criticism, she had the last laugh by winning the championship.
 
 
• हिंदी में: सभी आलोचनाओं के बावजूद, उसने चैंपियनशिप जीतकर अंत में सफल हुई।
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

__
 
• **To be the worst example of something **(किसी चीज़ का सबसे खराब उदाहरण होना):

 
 
• **Example:** The company is the worst example of how to manage resources.
 
• हिंदी में: कंपनी संसाधनों को प्रबंधित करने का सबसे खराब उदाहरण है।
 
 
 
• **To solve all the problems of life **(जीवन की सभी समस्याओं को हल करना):
 
 
• **Example:** Winning the lottery won't solve all the problems of life.
 
• हिंदी में: लॉटरी जीतने से जीवन की सभी समस्याएं हल नहीं होंगी।
 
 
 
• **To laugh at someone secretly **(किसी पर गुप्त रूप से हंसना):
 
 
• **Example:** They laughed at his mistakes secretly.
 
• हिंदी में: उन्होंने उसकी गलतियों पर गुप्त रूप से हंसा।

Despite their differences, the counties found common ground and __buried the hatchet__.

options.text: To seek revenge in the future

questions.solution: The correct answer is: **Option 3**. (मतभेदों को समाप्त करना और मेल-मिलाप करना) • **Example: **After years of rivalry, the two companies decided to bury the hatchet and collaborate on a new project. • **"To continue a conflict"** means to keep on fighting or disagreeing. (सार्वजनिक रूप से असहमति व्यक्त करना) • **Example: **The politicians disagreed publicly on the new policy. • **"To seek revenge in the future"** means to plan to get back at someone later. questions.question:
**Identify the correct meaning of the idiom(s) given below.**

At the drop of a hat
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "Without any hesitation; immediately.**"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The idiom 'At the drop of a hat' is used to describe a situation where something is done **instantly**, without any delay, or **without a significant reason.**
 
• It means doing something immediately, without hesitation.
 
• For example, if we say, "He would leave work** at the drop of a hat **to help his family," it means he would leave work immediately without hesitation to assist his family if needed.
 
• Hence, the correct answer will be **Option 2.**

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Hold the fort

options.text: To avoid being found guilty of a crime
To take responsibility for a situation temporarily

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **To take responsibility for a situation temporarily**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The idiom "Hold the fort" means to have responsibility for something while someone else is absent. (किसी और के अनुपस्थित रहने पर किसी चीज़ की ज़िम्मेदारी लेना)

 
 
• For example- *I’m going abroad for a few weeks, and Raju will hold the fort while I’m away.*
 
 
 
• So, it is clear that the most appropriate meaning of the idiom "Hold the fort" is "**To take responsibility for a situation temporarily**."
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is option 4.
